headline: Approved variances for 31 Cedar Street and a six-month extension for 75 North Street; appeal on 1-3 East Collins Street failed.
summary: Neighbors spoke against the plan for 7 Burnside Street and 5 Skerry Street Court, citing parking and density, and the applicant withdrew it. The 31 Cedar Street plan keeps the existing two-family home and moves a historic house from Washington Street to 27-29 Cedar Street. Residents raised drainage and snow storage concerns, and the approval added two special conditions to protect the retaining wall at 8 Fairfield Street.
decisions: Withdrew the 7 Burnside Street and 5 Skerry Street Court variance request without prejudice, 3-0.
Approved variances for 31 Cedar Street, 5-0, with standard and special conditions.
Motion to approve Charles Knight's appeal of the 1-3 East Collins Street permit failed, 0-5.
Approved a six-month extension for the 75 North Street development, 5-0.
Approved updated application requirements and standard conditions, 5-0.
Approved the September 9, 2026 meeting minutes as drafted and amended.
Approved the September 16, 2026 meeting minutes as drafted.

City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
October 21, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Zoning Board of Appeals (“Salem ZBA”) was held on Wednesday, October 
21, 2026 at 6:30 pm via remote participation in accordance with Section 30A of Chapter 20 of the Acts of 
2021, as amended by Section 40 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023, and further amended by Section 1 of Chapter 
2 of the Acts of 2025, the City is authorized to conduct remote meetings of its public bodies through June 30, 
2027.  
 
Chair Vyedin calls the meeting to order at 6:30 pm. 
Chair Vyedin explains how individuals can participate in the meeting remotely via Zoom, and that 
instructions to participate remotely can also be found on the Salem website.  Ms. Vyedin also 
explains the rules regarding public comment. 
 
ROLL CALL  
Those present were: Chair Nina Vyedin, Vice Chair Christa McGaha, Ellen Simpson, Hilary Forbes, 
Elena Eimert, Stephen Larrick, and Samantha Stringfellow.  Also in attendance were Brennan 
Postich — Staff Planner, Omar Bennani — Assistant City Solicitor, and Voula Orfanos — Building 
Commissioner.  Those absent were: Peter Habib. 
 
CONTINUANCES   
Location: 7 Burnside Street and 5 Skerry Street Court (Map 36, Lot 0157; Map 36, Lot 0149) 
(R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Graham Wing (formerly Graham Hines) 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of GRAHAM WING 
(formerly Graham Hines) at 7 BURNSIDE STREET and 5 SKERRY STREET 
COURT (Map 36, Lot 0157; Map 36, Lot 0149) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance 
per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to 
divide an existing merged parcel and construct a two-family house at 5 Skerry Street 
Court. The proposal would create a 4,393-square-foot lot at 7 Burnside Street with a 
2,196-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, and a 3,820-square-foot lot at 5 Skerry 
Street Court with a 1,910-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, thirty-seven-foot 
frontage, and insufficient front, side, and rear setbacks. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition.  Vice Chair McGaha recuses herself from the petition due to 
perceived potential conflict of interest.  Ms. Vyedin notes the three voting members, as two board 
members missed too many of the initial meetings to sign a Mullin Affidavit. 
 
Attorney Ryan Carlucci introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and confirms there is no 
potential for a quorum vote.  Mr. Carlucci states the petitioner would like to continue to a future
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 21, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  2 
meeting.  Chair Vyedin explains that there is no fifth person to bring in because two new members 
have missed too many of the sessions to vote on the matter.  She notes the difficulty in getting 
anything more than a four-member quorum, and suggests another option is to withdraw without 
prejudice and reapply with a new petition.  She acknowledges and apologizes for the difficulty of the 
circumstances.  The Board members discuss fees and re-advertising requirements.  Mr. Carlucci 
expresses a desire to withdraw without prejudice but notes that any Board feedback would be 
helpful regarding plan options and designs. 
 
Mr.  Larrick states he appreciates the parking study provided.  Ms. Simpson states she appreciates 
the information regarding trees and green space.  The Board members acknowledge the difficult 
situation, and Ms. Simpson states that after further consideration, she is more open to some of the 
proposed options but also highlights some of the neighbors’ concerns, such as drainage and snow. 
Ms. Simpson also discusses attempts to preserve existing trees and focusing on native plants for the 
landscaping.  Ms. Vyedin provides feedback regarding parking, and the Board continues to discuss 
the options within the proposal and neighborhood concerns.  The petitioners and Board members 
ask clarifying questions and discuss the proposal further, as well as steps required for approvals. 
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comments. 
 
Abigail Clark of 3 Skerry Street Court introduces herself as an abutter and states she is opposed to 
this project, stating the plans have inconsistencies, particularly with respect to the actual setbacks 
and property lines.  She questions the many continuances and the options and alleged 
inconsistencies, suggesting it is confusing and difficult to tell what relief is actually being sought and 
what is being proposed.  Ms. Clark speaks against the proposal and highlights many concerns with 
the petition, including parking and density. 
 
Gretchen Buckley introduces herself as an abutter on the Skerry Street side.  She states she provided 
comments in a letter and speaks to neighborhood concerns regarding the size and height of the 
proposal in such a small, dense neighborhood.  Ms. Buckley also questions the legal validity of 
subdividing the lot after it was merged to become more conforming.  She suggests getting 
professional and legal opinions with respect to any plans being proposed, arguing that accuracy and 
transparency are an issue.  She also suggests conditions for any potential approval, such as tree 
removal and an assessment of her home pre-construction, as she states she is certain that damage 
will be done to her property. 
 
Ian Clark of 3 Skerry Street Court introduces himself as an abutter and expresses opposition to the 
proposed variances.  Mr. Clark acknowledges the need for housing in Salem but states that there are 
better options available that do not require so many variances and such a large footprint on a small 
park.  Mr. Clark expressed various concerns and also asked questions about petitioners presenting 
multiple options and whether it makes it clear for commenters and concerned neighbors to know 
what is actually being proposed. 
 
A public commenter (no name or address provided) states that Mr. Hines advertises in his Airbnb 
post that parking in the neighborhood can be limited, and that he is misrepresenting the number of 
parking spaces available on Skerry St. Court.  The commenter expresses concerns and general 
opposition.  She also suggests the soil should be tested on the property.

  3 
Gigi (no last name provided) of 4 Skerry Street Court expresses opposition to the proposal and 
discusses various concerns. 
 
Mr. Carlucci requests to withdraw without prejudice. 
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Larrick motions to withdraw without prejudice the petition of GRAHAM 
WING (formerly Graham Hines) at 7 BURNSIDE STREET and 5 SKERRY STREET COURT 
(Map 36, Lot 0157; Map 36, Lot 0149) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 
Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to divide an existing merged parcel and 
construct a two-family house at 5 Skerry Street Court. The proposal would create a 4,393-square-
foot lot at 7 Burnside Street with a 2,196-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, and a 3,820-square-
foot lot at 5 Skerry Street Court with a 1,910-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, thirty-seven-foot 
frontage, and insufficient front, side, and rear setbacks.  
 
Ms. Simpson seconds the motion.  The vote is three (3) in favor (Ellen Simpson, Stephen 
Larrick, and Nina Vyedin) and none (0) opposed.  The motion passes. 
 
   
Location: 31 Cedar Street Avenue (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: 31 Cedar Street, LLC and Salem Residential Properties, LLC, through Michael 
Becker 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of1 CEDAR STREET, LLC 
and SALEM RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTIES, LLC, through MICHAEL 
BECKER, at 31 CEDAR STREET (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning District) for 
Variances per Section 3.2.4(3) Accessory Structures, Section 4.1.1 Dimensional 
Requirements, and Section 5.1.6(2) Parking Setbacks of the Salem Zoning Ordinance 
to permit the separate development of two existing record parcels; retain the existing 
two-family dwelling at 31-33 Cedar Street; and relocate the historic dwelling at 259 
Washington Street to 27-29 Cedar Street, retain the existing garage, and construct an 
addition to create a 2.5-story, two-family dwelling. Relief under Section 4.1.1 is 
requested for lot frontage, lot width, lot area, lot area per dwelling unit, lot coverage, 
and front and side setbacks on both parcels. Relief under Section 3.2.4(3) is requested 
for the side and rear setbacks of the existing detached accessory garage on 27-29 Cedar 
Street. Relief under Section 5.1.6(2) is requested to allow the surfaced shared driveway 
and parking-access areas to extend to the common lot line. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Michael Becker introduces himself and notes he is accompanied by his attorney, AJ Capano, and 
architect Sanir Lutfija.  AJ Capano introduces himself and presents changes to the initial plans.  
Renderings and elevations of the proposal are shown, as well as floor plans and plot plans.  Mr. 
Lutfija discusses the project as a whole to move/relocate the historic home from Washington Street
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 21, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  4 
and add an addition.  The petitioners indicate they have addressed previous concerns regarding snow 
storage/removal and spacing and discuss the parking proposal as well.  Additional plans are 
reviewed, as well as landscaping plans. 
 
The Board members discuss the plan updates and ask clarifying questions.  They also discuss the 
relief being requested.  The end result of the proposal will be to have two two-family dwellings.  
Additional renderings are presented with the updated proposal.  Ms. Simpson asks the petitioners 
how they feel about Historic Salem Inc.’s comments suggesting the historic home should not 
become a part of a new construction.  She asks if there was any consideration of keeping the historic 
house in the front as a separate unit and having a second unit behind it without raising the historic 
home.  Mr. Becker explains the reasoning behind the proposal, including making the spaces as 
livable as possible.  Board members ask about the layout of the historic property.  Mr. Becker 
continues to explain the proposal and the need for family-sized units.  Board members ask 
additional clarifying questions, and Mr. Becker discusses the neighborhood characteristics and 
benefits of the proposal.  Photos of the historic home are presented in its current location.   
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comments. 
 
Patricia MacDonald of 8 Fairfield Street introduces herself as a direct abutter.  She states her family 
has owned her property for many years, and she has concerns about her property being protected if 
relief is granted.  She asks for special conditions to follow precedent set in 1987, where the Board set 
the conditions in place to protect the retaining walls.  Ms. MacDonald also requests that a civil 
engineer design a permanent stormwater management system such as a dry well or continuous 
french drain to prevent water damage on other properties.  She states the condition was 
recommended in 2023 pursuant to drainage issues in the area.  Ms. MacDonald asks that the Board 
examine the snow storage space, claiming it is inadequate for winters where there is a lot of snow.  
She also asks that any trees be planted at mature height away from any walls, and that any other 
vegetation needs to be kept away from the wall as well to prevent root system damage.  Ms. 
MacDonald also requests a no-load zone, where excavated soil and heavy vehicles cannot be placed 
during construction, identified by a structural engineer.  She expresses concerns about the shared 
property boundary and potential detriment to her property. 
 
Sean O’Brian (no address provided) introduces himself and states that the Board member previously 
requested pictures of this lot.  He notes that a neighbor took some panoramic photos and sent them 
in with comments.  Mr. O’Brian expresses concerns about parking in the area.  Mr. O’Brian also 
speaks against the subdivision of the lot, as he contends it will take a nonconforming property and 
make it further nonconforming.  He also speaks to the condition of landscaping and green space. 
 
The Board members discuss the requested special conditions and petition, as well as findings related 
to the requested variances. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. Simpson motions to approve the petition of 1 CEDAR STREET, LLC and 
SALEM RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTIES, LLC, through MICHAEL BECKER, at 31 
CEDAR STREET (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning District) for Variances per Section 3.2.4(3) 
Accessory Structures, Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements, and Section 5.1.6(2) Parking 
Setbacks of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to permit the separate development of two existing record 
parcels; retain the existing two-family dwelling at 31-33 Cedar Street; and relocate the historic 
dwelling at 259 Washington Street to 27-29 Cedar Street, retain the existing garage, and construct an
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 21, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  5 
addition to create a 2.5-story, two-family dwelling. Relief under Section 4.1.1 is requested for lot 
frontage, lot width, lot area, lot area per dwelling unit, lot coverage, and front and side setbacks on 
both parcels. Relief under Section 3.2.4(3) is requested for the side and rear setbacks of the existing 
detached accessory garage on 27-29 Cedar Street. Relief under Section 5.1.6(2) is requested to allow 
the surfaced shared driveway and parking-access areas to extend to the common lot line.  The 
approval is subject to the following standard conditions: 
 
1. Petitioner shall comply with all city and state statutes, ordinances, codes, and regulations. 
2. All construction shall be done as per the plans and dimensions submitted to and 
approved by the Building Commissioner. 
3. All requirements of the Salem Fire Department relative to smoke and fire safety shall be 
strictly adhered to. 
4. Petitioner shall obtain a building permit prior to beginning any construction. 
5. The exterior finishes of new construction shall be in harmony with the existing structure. 
6. A Certificate of Occupancy is to be obtained. 
7. A Certificate of Inspection is to be obtained 
8. Petitioner is to obtain approval from any City Board or Commission having jurisdiction 
including, but not limited to, the Planning Board. 
9. Petitioner shall obtain street numbering from the City of Salem Assessor’s Office and 
shall display said number to be visible from the street. 
10. Unless this Decision expressly provides otherwise, any zoning relief granted does not 
empower or authorize the Petitioner to demolish or reconstruct the structure(s) located 
on the subject property to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area or 
more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost at the time of destruction.  If the 
structure is demolished by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its 
replacement cost or more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area at the time of 
destruction, it shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with the provisions of the 
Ordinance. 
11. All construction shall be done per the plans and dimension submitted to and approved 
by this Board.  Any modification to the plans and dimensions must be approved by the 
Board of Appeals unless such changes are deemed a minor field change by the Building 
Commissioner in consultation with the Chair of the Board of Appeals. 
12. Petitioner shall schedule Assessing Department inspections of the property, at least 
annually, to project completion and a final inspection upon project completion. 
 
And the following special conditions: 
  1.  A surveyor and engineer shall conduct an existing conditions survey of the retaining  
       wall abutting 8 Fairfield Street prior to the issuance of a building permit from the  
       Inspectional Services Department. 
  2.  The petitioner shall hold the owners of 8 Fairfield Street harmless in the event that any  
       damage is caused as a direct result of construction of the proposed two-family structure.  
      An engineer shall submit a letter verifying the conditions of the retaining wall, and  
       actions taken from damage, if any, prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy from  
       the Inspectional Services Department. 
 
Ms. Stringfellow seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Nina Vyedin, Christa 
McGaha, Stephen Larrick, Samantha Stringfellow, and Ellen Simpson) and none (0) 
opposed.  The motion passes.

REGULAR AGENDA   
Location: 1-3 East Collins Street (Map 36, Lot 0277) (R1 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Charles Knight 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of CHARLES KNIGHT 
regarding the property located at 1-3 EAST COLLINS STREET (Map 36, Lot 0277) 
(R1 Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) to appeal the Building 
Commissioner’s decision to permit a building over thirty-five feet tall, and a dumpster 
located less than four feet from the abutting property line. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition for administrative appeal and asks if there have been any 
changes or if anything has been built not according to the permit.  She notes a statement from the 
project architect indicating that construction was consistent with permits granted, and Ms. Orfanos 
explains that the construction was consistent with plans that were permitted.   
 
Charles Knight introduces himself and explains the initial approval from the Board, and indicates 
the variances were granted including approval of a third story as long as the height was under 35 feet 
tall.  Mr. Knight states that one corner of the home is 37.5 feet tall and suggests it is not at low mean 
grade.  He suggests the building is too tall and that the state requirement for a dumpster is 10 feet 
from a residence.  Mr. Knight also indicates a certificate of occupancy was granted prior to any sign-
off from DEP or related to Chapter 91.  He suggests the sequence of events was improper, and that 
should null and void the approval. 
 
Ms. Orfanos indicates the City’s conservation agent coordinated with DEP, and it was all signed off 
prior to the certificate of occupancy.  Ms. Orfanos also states the permit was issued for 51 feet.  She 
provides additional information and indicates there were no deviations from the plan and that all 
required departments signed off prior to any building approval.   
 
The Board discusses the matter and confirms the permit is for more than 35 feet.  Mr. Knight says 
the Board can do what they need to do, and he will appeal this decision as well. 
 
Attorney Benjamin Fierro introduces himself on behalf of the project owners.  Mr. Fierro discusses 
the Dover Amendment and the Americans with Disabilities Act, as well as the project history and its 
non-profit educational use.   
 
The Board discusses the matter briefly.  Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment. 
 
Steve Kapantais of Wysteria Street introduces himself and states he is not an abutter to the project, 
but that he fully understands the Chapter 91 licensing process.  Mr. Kapantais contends the project 
has not been signed off for a Chapter 91 license.  He states the walkway is required to be five feet in
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 21, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  7 
width but suggests that the actual width is less.  Mr. Kapantais also suggests language should be used 
carefully, and states that when the chair of a meeting makes a statement about making findings, 
which is improper, as they can have opinions, but the Board as a whole makes findings.  Mr. 
Kapantais contends that otherwise it sounds totalitarian. 
 
The Board discusses that matter further and notes that no documentation or support for the 
appellants’ claims has been provided. 
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Larrick motions to approve the petition of CHARLES KNIGHT regarding 
the property located at 1-3 EAST COLLINS STREET (Map 36, Lot 0277) (R1 Zoning District; 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) to appeal the Building Commissioner’s decision to permit a 
building over thirty-five feet tall, and a dumpster located less than four feet from the abutting 
property line. 
 
Ms. Simpson seconds the motion.  The vote is zero (0) in favor, and five (5) opposed (Stephen 
Larrick, Christa McGaha, Ellen Simpson, Nina Vyedin, and Samantha Stringfellow).  The 
motion does not pass.

September 9, 2026

OLD/NEW BUSINESS  
 
Location: 75 North Street, 2 Commercial Street, and 3 South Mason Street (Map 26, Lot

Applicant: 75 North Street, LLC
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals

Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of 75 NORTH STREET 
LLC at 75 NORTH STREET, 2 COMMERCIAL STREET, and 3 SOUTH MASON 
STREET (Map 26, Lot 0058; Map 26, Lot 0057; Map 26, Lot 0054) (North River Canal 
Corridor Neighborhood Mixed Use District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) for a 
six-month extension to rights granted by the Board in a decision dated December 11,

Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Ryan Carlucci introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and explains that there have 
been no changes to the proposal, but that a six-month extension is being requested while the state 
finalizes the Chapter 91 review. 
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Larrick motions to approve the petition of 75 NORTH STREET LLC at 75 
NORTH STREET, 2 COMMERCIAL STREET, and 3 SOUTH MASON STREET (Map 26, Lot 
0058; Map 26, Lot 0057; Map 26, Lot 0054) (North River Canal Corridor Neighborhood Mixed Use 
District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) for a six-month extension to rights granted by the 
Board in a decision dated December 11, 2023, for Variances per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional 
Requirements, Section 8.4.9 and 8.4.9(c) Parking Requirements, and Section 8.4.13(4) Transitional 
Overlay District to construct a sixty-unit, four-story, mixed-use development with relief requested 
for lot area per dwelling unit, one-to-one parking ratios, and 100-foot and fifty-foot buffer entrance 
and landscaping requirements.  
 
Ms. McGaha seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Nina Vyedin, Christa McGaha, 
Stephen Larrick, Ellen Simpson, and Hilary Forbes) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes. 
 
   
Introductions for Associate Member Samantha Stringfellow 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces Samantha Stringfellow and Board members welcome her. 
 
Staff Updates on the Board’s Application Requirements and Standard Conditions 
 
Chair Vyedin discusses and reviews the staff updates to the application requirements and standard
